description: Named competitors, how you beat them, and what your own pipeline says about whether that's working. The win/loss columns are computed from opportunities — not opinion.

columns.name: aliases
columns.note: Other names they appear under in deal records, semicolon-separated. Matching fails without these.

columns.name: tier
columns.note: Primary = shows up in deals regularly and you lose to them. Reserve it; a long Primary list means none of them get real attention.

columns.name: category
columns.note: What kind of alternative: direct rival, adjacent tool, in-house build, do-nothing

columns.name: their_pitch
columns.note: How they describe themselves, in their words not yours

columns.name: their_strengths
columns.note: Where they genuinely win. A battlecard that claims a competitor has no strengths gets a rep ambushed.

columns.name: our_win_themes
columns.note: What actually wins against them, ideally traced to won deals

columns.name: landmines
columns.note: Questions that surface their weaknesses without you naming them

columns.name: do_not_say
columns.note: Claims that are wrong, stale, or legally risky. As valuable as the win themes.

columns.name: deals_met
columns.note: DERIVED from opportunities where this competitor is named

columns.name: deals_won
columns.note: DERIVED

columns.name: deals_lost
columns.note: DERIVED

columns.name: deals_open
columns.note: DERIVED

columns.name: win_rate
columns.note: DERIVED: won / (won + lost), as a percentage. Blank when the sample is too small to mean anything.

columns.name: sample_note
columns.note: DERIVED. Says so plainly when the sample is too small — 2 wins from 3 deals is not a 67% win rate.

columns.name: avg_deal_size
columns.note: DERIVED: average amount when they're in the deal

columns.name: last_seen_date
columns.note: DERIVED: most recent deal they appeared in

columns.name: trend
columns.note: DERIVED: last two quarters against the two before

columns.name: where_we_win
columns.note: DERIVED where possible: segments and use cases with the best record against them

columns.name: where_they_win
columns.note: DERIVED where possible

columns.name: common_loss_reason
columns.note: DERIVED from loss reasons on deals they were in

columns.name: last_signal_date
columns.note: DERIVED: most recent market signal about this competitor

columns.name: signals_90d
columns.note: DERIVED: signal count in the last 90 days. A quiet competitor and a busy one need different attention.

columns.name: signals_since_battlecard
columns.note: DERIVED: signals logged since last_researched. THE staleness measure — a battlecard is out of date because specific things happened, not because time passed. Non-zero on a Primary competitor means refresh before the next call.

columns.name: latest_signal
columns.note: DERIVED: headline and date of the most recent signal, so the registry is readable without opening the market log

columns.name: open_impacts
columns.note: DERIVED: distinct competitive_impact values from signals since the battlecard was written, semicolon-separated

columns.name: battlecard_path
columns.note: Relative path to the battlecard markdown

columns.name: watch_id
columns.note: Links to the market watchlist entry that monitors them
